prompts.sourceFeedback: An orbital is a region of space around the nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron. It can hold up to two electrons with opposite spins; it is not a fixed path around the nucleus.
prompts.sourceAnswer: A region of space around the nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron. Each orbital can hold up to two electrons with opposite spins.

prompts.sourcePrompt: What is the name given to a region of space around the nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
prompts.pupilPrompt: What is the name given to a region of space around the nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
prompts.sourceFeedback: An atomic orbital describes the region where an electron is likely to be found, rather than an orbit or fixed electron path.

prompts.sourcePrompt: What is the name given to a group of orbitals of the same type within an electron shell, such as s, p, d or f orbitals.
prompts.pupilPrompt: What is the name given to a group of orbitals of the same type within an electron shell, such as s, p, d or f orbitals.
prompts.sourceFeedback: A subshell groups orbitals of the same type within a shell. For example, the 2p subshell contains three p orbitals.

prompts.sourcePrompt: What is the name given to a group of orbitals with the same principal quantum number, broadly associated with a particular energy and distance from the nucleus.
prompts.pupilPrompt: What is the name given to a group of orbitals with the same principal quantum number, broadly associated with a particular energy and distance from the nucleus.
prompts.sourceFeedback: Orbitals with the same principal quantum number belong to one electron shell. For example, 2s and 2p orbitals belong to the second shell.
Ionic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between positive and negative ions. Electron transfer forms ions; the bond itself is the attraction between them.
prompts.sourceAnswer: The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

prompts.sourcePrompt: How many s orbitals exist in each electron shell?
prompts.pupilPrompt: How many s orbitals exist in each electron shell?
prompts.sourceFeedback: Each s subshell contains one orbital, so it can hold up to two electrons.

prompts.sourcePrompt: How many p orbitals exist in each electron shell?
prompts.pupilPrompt: How many orbitals are there in one p subshell?
prompts.sourceFeedback: A p subshell contains three orbitals and holds up to six electrons. A p subshell exists from the second shell onwards; the first shell has only an s subshell.

prompts.sourcePrompt: How many d orbitals exist in each electron shell?
prompts.pupilPrompt: How many orbitals are there in one d subshell?
prompts.sourceFeedback: A d subshell contains five orbitals and holds up to ten electrons. A d subshell exists from the third shell onwards.

prompts.sourcePrompt: What type of structure do all ionic compounds have?
prompts.pupilPrompt: What type of structure do solid ionic compounds have?
prompts.sourceFeedback: The source answer applies to solid ionic compounds. The ordered lattice is disrupted on melting or dissolving.
A covalent bond is the strong electrostatic attraction between a shared pair of electrons and the nuclei of the bonded atoms.
prompts.sourceAnswer: The electrostatic attraction between a shared pair of electrons and 2 positive nuclei.

prompts.sourceFeedback: Periodicity describes the repeating pattern in properties as atomic number increases. This linked recall card comes from the supplied set and connects electron structure to the Periodicity topic.
prompts.sourceAnswer: Repeating pattern in the physical and chemical properties of elements when arranged in order of increasing atomic number

prompts.sourcePrompt: Define the term: giant ionic lattice
prompts.pupilPrompt: Define the term: giant ionic lattice
prompts.sourceFeedback: A giant ionic lattice is a repeating, three-dimensional arrangement of positive and negative ions. The particles are ions, not neutral atoms or molecules.
prompts.sourceAnswer: A repeating pattern of oppositely charged ions

prompts.sourcePrompt: Define the term: dative / coordinate bond?
prompts.pupilPrompt: Define the term: dative / coordinate bond?
prompts.sourceFeedback: In a dative covalent or coordinate bond, one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair. Once formed, it is a covalent bond.
prompts.sourceAnswer: A covalent bond in which both electrons in the shared pair are donated by the same atom.

prompts.sourcePrompt: Define the term: average bond enthalpy.
prompts.pupilPrompt: Define the term: average bond enthalpy.
prompts.sourceFeedback: Average bond enthalpy is the energy required to break one mole of a specified covalent bond in gaseous molecules, averaged over different compounds. It measures covalent bond strength and links to the Enthalpy topic.
prompts.sourceAnswer: the energy required to break one mole of a specified covalent bond in gaseous molecules, averaged over a range of different compounds.
